bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for LNG and keg capacity; maintaining net cash position (INR275cr available); no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on organic growth and strategic order execution
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Keg volume ramp-up delayed vs internal targets; LNG station rollout slower than policy potential; execution risk on ITER project (long duration); global trade policy shifts (US tariffs); competitive pressure from Chinese players in kegs (mitigated by antidumping duties)
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; emphasized technological leadership, global approvals, and policy tailwinds; tone on LNG and kegs is bullish; ITER and CO2 battery framed as strategic differentiators, not one-offs
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The INR28,000cr Q2FY26 keg order (pre-announced) is likely a cumulative pipeline value, not a single order — indicating strong pre-commitments from global brewers; ITER’s 200 CTS panels represent a multi-year, high-margin, repeatable workstream beyond the INR145cr order; CO2 battery order from Italy signals export-ready clean energy tech, not just domestic
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Strong Balance Sheet (Net Debt Free)" with net debt defined in the deck as "[Gross Debt incl. short term] Less [Cash & Bank, FDR & Mutual Fund]", all formulae stated to be as per the definition in the RHP.
- "Availability of Approx Rs 331 Cr Free Cash"; net cash/bank balance is higher than Mar'26 despite payment of dividend, helped by an increase in advances from customers and realization of contract assets/trade receivables.
- Growth and capex are funded internally: "Debt-free and strong net worth; Savli plant funded from internal accruals" and "Strong liquidity and robust operational cash flow to support growth & capex".
- Treasury is run for carry rather than debt reduction: finance cost is higher because of "not liquidating the Long Term Mutual Fund to save taxes and utilizing the fund based limit to get benefit of differential gain of around 0.75% in earning vs cost of funds", so the deck argues there is "no increase in Net Finance cost in real terms".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Industrial Gas: 48% of revenue; led by ultra-high-purity ammonia containers (first in India, 11 units ordered) and CO2 battery storage (first order, 26 units); LNG: 29% of revenue; 145 tanks dispatched, capacity expansion to 5,000-6,000 tanks/year by end-FY26; Cryo Scientific: 19% of revenue; INR145cr ITER order (90% in-house fabrication); Beverage Kegs: low base but accelerating; 6.4cr Q1 orders, Q2 FY26 orders at INR28,000cr (pre-announced), global approvals from Heineken & AB InBev secured, Asahi/Carlsberg audits scheduled for Sep-Oct 2025
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Self-described as the "World's leading provider of customized cryogenic equipment" with "Over 30 years of experience in design, manufacturing and installation of cryogenic equipment" and, under Key Strengths, the "Largest supplier of cryogenic equipment in India".
- Global reach: "5000+ customers across 100+ countries", 3 countries with INOXCVA operations and 30+ sales & service support locations; key export geographies listed as US, Europe, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, Korea, UAE, Australia and Bangladesh.
- Entry barrier claimed from a third-party source: "Stringency related to design, manufacturing and the number of regulations in the cryogenic equipment segment is a barrier to entry" (footnoted to Crisil report Nov23), reinforced by approvals including ASME U & R Stamp, DOT 39, EN 13458/EN 13530, CE, IATF 16949, FSSC 22000, ISO 3824-Part 2 and AS9100 D Aerospace.
- Stated vision: "To be the world's best integrated cryogenic solutions enterprise with a leadership position across products and markets, exceeding customer and stakeholder expectations", supported by six growth pillars including "introducing products ahead of demand".
- Resilience framing of "Multiple Geographies, Multiple Sectors, Multiple Products" spanning "Steel to Space", "Healthcare to Hydrogen" and "Paper To Power".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order intake] "Highest ever Order booking" of Rs 532 Cr in Q1FY27 (Actual orders received Rs 532 Cr vs Rs 415 Cr in Q1FY26, +28.4%), which the deck notes "includes high value order of Rs 217 Cr from US major private Aerospace Co. (IG)"; the Q1FY26 base included an ITER France order of Rs 146 Cr for CTS Repair (CSD). Q1FY27 order mix: IG 72%, LNG 16%, CSD 10%, Other 2%.
- [Aerospace / space] Secured AS9100 Aerospace Certification serving aviation, space and defence; an additional order from a US space company for large size (1000M3) tanks and a high-value repeat order from a global aerospace company; the 2024 milestone records an order for largest size (1500M3) tanks in the IG segment from a US space company. The deck also details INOXCVA's role in ISRO test-facility and launchpad systems.
- [Big science] Secured an order for 22 Nos of cryogenic modules for CERN's HL-LHC project, plus an additional ITER order for installation of Cryo & Warm line and refurbishment of the Lower Cryostat Thermal Shield; ITER First Plasma is cited as expected in 2035 and India is described as developing a 25-year fusion roadmap with two new tokamak machines before an Indian DEMO in the late 2040s.
- [Partnerships] Agreement with Wayout to explore a freshwater infra system for the Asian market, and a collaboration with ITMBU for skill development in orbital welding and semiconductor industries; India's semiconductor push (ISM) is flagged as an adjacent opportunity.
- [Headwind stated] "Sales were marginally lower on YoY basis primarily due to ongoing logistics disruptions arising from the geopolitical situation involving Iran and the Gulf region"; other income also fell 14.7% as forex gain dropped to Rs 0.3 Cr from Rs 2.9 Cr.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Higher margins in new products: ultra-purity ammonia and CO2 battery storage (premium pricing); cost pressures mitigated by antidumping duties on Chinese kegs; Savli plant costs front-loaded (stabilizing by Q4FY26); steel tariff impact on US cylinders limited to material cost only (50% of price), EBIT margin remains 14-15%
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 18-20% YoY; margin: stable EBITDA margin target of ~25%; order inflow: expects strong Q2-Q4 inflow from LNG, Cryo, and keg segments; capex/commissioning: INR80cr total capex for FY26, including INR5-6cr for LNG tank capacity expansion at Kalol, Savli plant stabilization by Q4FY26
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR1,457cr as of Jun 30, 2025; 63% export content; major components: INR145cr ITER Cryostat Thermal Shield order (2-year duration), 11 ultra-high-purity ammonia containers (2 delivered, 9 in production), 145 LNG fuel tanks dispatched, 28,000cr keg orders received in Q2FY26 (pre-announced)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: LNG fueling station ecosystem (Adani/Ambani land conversion policy), SMR nuclear reactor manufacturing (bidding with govt partners), hydrogen equipment scaling, CO2 battery commercialization (global replication potential), keg volume ramp-up (3-4x current size target by FY28)
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: INOX India delivered strong Q1FY26 growth with 16.7% revenue rise, driven by breakthrough orders in ultra-high-purity ammonia containers and India’s first CO2 battery storage system, while LNG and keg segments show scalable momentum; the company’s diversified high-margin product portfolio and strategic capex expansion position it to capture India’s clean energy transition and global industrial supply chain reshoring.

open.item: Company reiterated it is a consistent dividend-paying company and will consider a dividend at year-end, having a comfortable net cash of Rs.191 crore.

open.horizon: FY26 final dividend, pending AGM approval
open.item: Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 2 per equity share (100% of Rs 2 face value) for FY26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.

Management flagged US tariffs (35%) as a tricky, changing issue but expects only a slight, not substantial, impact given US is ~10-12% of revenue and tariff applies only to the steel component of cylinders.

ISRO/space tender for the third launch pad (total ~Rs.4,000 crore, cryogenic ~15-20% of it) expected to be out around December/early next year; company sees a better chance having done the second launch pad.

Secured global approval from Heineken (plus AB InBev already done); Carlsberg and Asahi audits scheduled for September/October, expected to unlock keg volume ramp; new distributors appointed in UK, Germany and US.
Company secured its first-of-its-kind Australia order (~Rs.21 crore) for oxygen/nitrogen/CO2 IMO containers with a challenging sub-6-month delivery timeline, committed to meeting it.
Company is qualified with Blue Energy (India's largest LNG-tank OEM) and expects to supply substantial equipment this year; mini LNG terminal order flow expected from the beginning of next year.

Executing first Highview Power (long-duration storage) project, delivery expected by end January/February; management expects more of Highview's 4-5 pipeline projects (to be completed by 2030) to start flowing from the beginning of next year.
open.promised: delivery Jan-Feb; new orders early CY26 text

open.item: Company is targeting at least 100,000 beverage kegs sold this year, with a vision to be 3-4x current size in 3-4 years.
Savli plant did ~Rs.200 crore last year and is planned for Rs.300-350 crore this year, with stabilization expected in about 6 months to 1 year; 150+ tanks currently under construction.
Company targets FY26 capex of around Rs.80 crore, mainly for Kandla facility expansion (1,500 cubic-meter vessels) plus Kalol and Savli.
Industrial Gas segment is expected to grow around 15%-17% in FY26 (8-10% conventional plus 5-6% from new products).
Management targets FY26 total revenue growth of about 18%-20%.
Company delivered 9 tanks (50-200 KL) to a US semiconductor customer and won an order from Tata's semiconductor complex in Assam to be supplied in FY26.
Existing capacity implies peak revenue potential of ~Rs.1,200-1,300 crore at Kalol/Kandla plus Rs.300-500 crore from Savli over 1-2 years (~Rs.1,800 crore max on current capacity).
Company secured an ITER Cryostat Thermal Shield order worth ~Rs.145 crore, with ~90% fabrication in-house and the project expected to span nearly 2 years.

Positioning as a critical enabler of India's hydrogen economy, targeting long-term demand for liquid hydrogen cryogenic tanks, transfer systems and distribution infrastructure under the National Green Hydrogen Mission (5 MMT annual green hydrogen production target by 2030).
Company aims to scale LNG fuel-tank capability up to 10x over the next few years, anticipating a need for 30,000-40,000 fuel tanks in 3-5 years.
As leading conglomerates set up 5 MTPA green hydrogen production capacity by 2030, ~20% of each project's revenue (liquid hydrogen storage/transport) is the addressable opportunity for INOX.

Extending addressable market into stainless steel beverage kegs (division launched FY25) in partnership with Supermonte Group, Italy, targeting global beverage producers phasing out single-use containers.

verdicts.item: Management assessed the recently imposed US tariffs as having very minimal/small impact, with the standard-tank exposure offset by a non-compete clause valid through end of 2028.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'the impact of this tariff, yes, slightly will be there, but not substantial for our products'; 'we have not seen any decline in the orders' — minimal-impact assessment reaffirmed; non-compet…

verdicts.item: Company won its first-of-its-kind liquid air energy storage order (~Rs.50 crore+, England customer) for a 60MW project, expected to be completed by 2026, opening up multiple similar projects.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'Highview Power. We are already executing one project... we are delivering by end of January or February... at least 4, 5 are there in the pipeline' — on track, not yet completed.

verdicts.item: From FY25 onwards, growth capex will be around Rs.40-50 crores plus Rs.15-20 crores maintenance capex per year.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'our Capex for this year, we have targeted around INR80 crores' — above the original 40-50 growth + 15-20 maintenance frame, and not broken into that split. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Company has submitted budgetary numbers for ISRO's proposed third launch pad and expects order movement once the government approves the budget.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'the tender is not yet out. Most likely, it is coming up in December or early next year... hopefully, by end of this year, something should come up for the third launch' — order movement push…

verdicts.item: Management guides ~18-20% revenue growth for FY26 (at least 20% above whatever FY25 revenue is achieved), with EBITDA margins of 21%-24%.
verdicts.note: Logar: 'our target is to have the turnover increase about 18% to 20% in this year'; Jaiveer asks 'do you retain your guidance of 18%, 20%?' — Acharya: 'Yes' — reaffirmed, Q1 tracking slightly below. […

verdicts.note: 'EBITDA was INR89 crores' on 'revenue of INR352 crores' — margin tracking within the guided range; FY26 ongoing. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Company started construction of a new cryo shop at Savli, spending around Rs.80 crores on new capex (machinery + building); Savli capacity to be raised to Rs.300-500 crore over 1-2 years.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'this year, we have plan of around INR300 crores, INR350 crores... more than 150 tanks are under construction at our Savli plant'. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Savli capacity-building/infrastructure expansion (incl. cryo shop) will be fully commissioned by end of March 2025, leaving no capacity stress for next year.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'stabilization will take around 6 months to 1 year' — commissioning done but full stabilization/no-capacity-stress state is still being reached, later than the end-Mar-2025 framing.

verdicts.item: Company plans Rs.80-100 crore capex in FY26 (similar to prior year) and is ready for next 2 years capacity-wise.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'our Capex for this year, we have targeted around INR80 crores... some expansion of our Kandla facility... Kalol and Savli'. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Company secured its largest-ever LNG order, a turnkey mini-LNG terminal in The Bahamas (15,000 metric ton storage, world's largest double-walled VI LNG tank) to be completed in about 12-14 months.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'we have been doing the LNG small-scale terminals at Bahamas now, and we already finished at Caribbean LNG' — Bahamas project underway, not yet completed.

verdicts.item: Beverage keg 9-month revenue was ~Rs.19 crore and management expects to end FY25 at ~Rs.30-35 crore (below earlier target); Savli plant total ~Rs.200 crore revenue this year.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'last year, we did almost INR200 crores from that plant' — the ~Rs.200 cr Savli portion confirmed; the Rs.30-35 cr keg figure is not restated. [±10% rule]

wtt.summary: 46% guidance hit (24 chains); 1/4 projects on-time; 24% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and expansive across all four segments; management reaffirmed 18-20% FY26 growth and downplayed US tariff impact, while candidly acknowledging keg volumes remain below internal expectations and the ITER Cryostat order is a one-off.

meta.thesis: INOX India delivered strong Q1FY26 growth with 16.7% revenue rise, driven by breakthrough orders in ultra-high-purity ammonia containers and India’s first CO2 battery storage system, while LNG and keg segments show scalable momentum; the company’s diversified high-margin product portfolio and strategic capex expansion position it to capture India’s clean energy transition and global industrial supply chain reshoring.
